title: Where to stay in Gangtok by budget
meta_description: Where to stay in Gangtok in 2026: the best areas, real hotels from hostels to Taj Guras Kutir and Mayfair, indicative prices, steps, heating and views.
summary: For most visitors the best place to stay in Gangtok is within a 10-minute walk of MG Marg, on Tibet Road, PS Road or Namnang Road, at about ₹1,500–8,000 a night. Couples who want space and a spa choose forest resorts such as Mayfair or Taj Guras Kutir at about ₹14,000–35,000. Prices are indicative.

sections.heading: Pick the area before the hotel
paras: Gangtok is a long town on a ridge, and the map lies about distance. A hotel 1 km from MG Marg as the crow flies can be a 25-minute climb, and a resort '6 km from town' can be 40 minutes away in evening traffic. So we always start with the area. If you want to walk to dinner and the taxi stands, stay close to MG Marg. If you want quiet and a garden, go to Paljor Stadium Road or the forest resorts and accept a car for every trip.

The table below is how we think about the town when we book rooms for guests. The prices are indicative ranges for a double room per night in 2026; they rise 20–40 percent in October, late December and May, and fall in the monsoon.

sections.heading: Budget: ₹1,500–3,000 a night
paras: Clean budget rooms are easy to find in the lanes behind MG Marg, on Tibet Road and in Development Area. Most have a private bathroom with a geyser, Wi-Fi of varying quality and a small restaurant or tie-up with one. What separates a good budget room from a bad one in Gangtok is heating, light and stairs: many cheap rooms face a wall, and many sit several floors below the road.

Hotel Mount Jopuno on PS Road, about 300 m from the centre, is a simple, central hotel with parking, which matters if you have a driver; we see it at about ₹2,500–4,500. Solo travellers and backpackers use Zostel Gangtok in Upper Sichey, near Tamang Gumpa, with dorm beds from about ₹500 and private rooms from about ₹1,800. Registered homestays on the outskirts, towards Ranka and the Rumtek road, cost about ₹1,200–2,500 per person with meals and suit slow travellers with a car.

Two more we like at the upper end of budget: Mintokling Guest House on Bhanu Path, a quiet, garden-fronted guest house about 10 minutes on foot from MG Marg, at about ₹2,500–4,000; and, for a night in the countryside, the village homestays of Martam, about an hour from town via Rumtek, at about ₹1,500–2,500 per person with meals.
list: Ask whether a room heater is included from November to February
Ask how many steps lead from the road to reception
Ask for a room with a window, not one facing a wall
Confirm the ₹50 Sikkim tourist fee is charged once and shown on the bill

sections.heading: Mid-range: ₹3,500–8,500 a night
paras: This is where most of our value and comfort guests stay, and Gangtok has a good choice. The Chumbi Residency on Tibet Road is a comfortable, well-run hotel a short walk above MG Marg, at about ₹6,000–9,500. Hotel Tashi Delek opens straight onto MG Marg itself; ask for an upper rear-facing room to avoid street noise. Hotel Sonam Delek on Tibet Road is a small, family-run hotel that sells rooms with windows facing the Kanchenjunga range, at about ₹2,500–4,500.

Summit Namnang Courtyard and Spa, about 10 minutes' walk below MG Marg, adds a spa at a mid-range price. Lemon Tree Hotel Gangtok in Middle Sichey offers branded standards, a lift and a restaurant, which families with grandparents value more than character, at about ₹4,000–8,000. The Royal Plaza in Upper Syari has larger rooms on a quieter side of town. For a last night before an early drive to Bagdogra, the hotels at Tadong on NH10 save 20–30 minutes.

For character, Netuk House on Tibet Road is a family-run heritage house built in the late 1950s, with Sikkimese rooms and home cooking, at about ₹4,000–7,000. Hotel Tibet on Paljor Stadium Road is a dependable, lift-equipped choice for families, at about ₹3,500–6,000, and The Hidden Forest Retreat in Middle Sichey is a family guest house set in gardens around an orchid nursery, at about ₹4,000–6,500.

sections.heading: Upmarket and heritage: ₹6,500–16,000
paras: The Elgin Nor-Khill on Paljor Stadium Road was built in the 1930s as the royal guest house of the Chogyals of Sikkim and is now a heritage hotel with gardens, a proper dining room and a spa. It suits older couples and anyone who likes a building with a past, at about ₹9,000–16,000. Denzong Regency at Cherry Banks, opposite Raj Bhawan, is a large four-star hotel with a spa and casino, bigger rooms and full facilities, at about ₹6,500–12,000.
Both are within a short taxi ride of MG Marg and quiet in the evening. Ask for a mountain-facing room in writing; the range is to the north-west, and only some rooms see it.

sections.heading: Forest resorts: ₹14,000–35,000
paras: Two resorts define premium Gangtok. Mayfair Spa Resort and Casino at Lower Samdur sits in a large forest estate below the town, 20–30 minutes from MG Marg, with a spa and casino; we see rooms at about ₹14,000–30,000. Taj Guras Kutir Resort and Spa at Pangthang, opened by IHCL in 2023 in the forest above Gangtok, has a J Wellness Circle spa and several restaurants and describes Kanchenjunga views; expect about ₹18,000–35,000. Both suit honeymooners and travellers who plan to spend real time at the hotel.

For a quieter, greener stay at a mid-range price, Bamboo Retreat at Sajong, off the road to Rumtek, is set among trees and organic gardens at about ₹4,000–7,500. The trade-off with all three is the same: every visit to town is a car ride, and dinner on MG Marg means a driver waiting.

sections.heading: Where to stay by traveller
paras: When guests ask us for one name, we ask them two questions back: how many nights, and who is travelling. These are our usual first suggestions, all real hotels operating as far as we know in 2026, with indicative prices for a double room per night. Rates change by season and booking channel, so treat them as a guide.

If you are adding North Sikkim, your Gangtok hotel does two extra jobs. It stores the bags you do not need up north, and it absorbs date changes if permits are held for weather. Choose one that keeps luggage for two or three nights at no charge, where the SUV can reach the door for a 9 am departure to Lachung.
list: First visit, two or three nights: The Chumbi Residency or Hotel Tashi Delek, about ₹4,500–9,500
Couple wanting a view in town: Hotel Sonam Delek, about ₹2,500–4,500
Family on a budget with a driver: Hotel Mount Jopuno, about ₹2,500–4,500
Family with grandparents: Lemon Tree Hotel Gangtok, about ₹4,000–8,000
Heritage lovers: The Elgin Nor-Khill, about ₹9,000–16,000
Honeymooners: Mayfair or Taj Guras Kutir, about ₹14,000–35,000
Solo backpackers: Zostel Gangtok, from about ₹500 a bed

sections.heading: Views, stairs, heating and booking
paras: Kanchenjunga is visible from Gangtok on clear mornings, mostly from October to April, and only from rooms facing north-west. Do not pay a large premium for a 'mountain view' in the monsoon, when the range is hidden for weeks. If your room faces the valley, Tashi View Point and Ganesh Tok are a short drive at dawn.

Access matters more than stars for families. Many Gangtok hotels are on steep lanes with stairs, limited parking and no lift, and taxis cannot drive on MG Marg. Heating matters from November to February, when nights fall to about 4–5 °C. And dates matter if you are going north: permits for Tsomgo and North Sikkim can be held for weather, which shifts your Gangtok nights, so a flexible rate is worth a little extra. Book 6–8 weeks ahead for October, Christmas and May; 1–2 weeks is enough in the monsoon and March. All prices here are indicative; check current rates before you travel. Tell us the dates and the kind of room you want, and we will check live availability rather than promising a room we have not confirmed.

faqs.q: Which is the best area to stay in Gangtok?
faqs.a: For a first visit, stay within a 10-minute walk of MG Marg, on Tibet Road, PS Road or Namnang Road, so you can walk to dinner and the taxi stands. Paljor Stadium Road is quieter but still central. Couples who want a spa and space choose forest resorts at Lower Samdur or Pangthang and accept a car for every trip into town.

faqs.q: What are the best luxury hotels in Gangtok?
faqs.a: Taj Guras Kutir Resort and Spa at Pangthang and Mayfair Spa Resort and Casino at Lower Samdur are the two forest resorts, at about ₹14,000–35,000 a night in 2026. The Elgin Nor-Khill, the 1930s royal guest house on Paljor Stadium Road, is the heritage choice, and Denzong Regency at Cherry Banks is a full-service four-star. Prices are indicative.

faqs.q: How much is a budget hotel in Gangtok?
faqs.a: About ₹1,500–3,000 a night for a clean double with a private bathroom in 2026, more in October, late December and May. Hostel beds at places such as Zostel Gangtok start around ₹500. Check heating from November to February, the number of steps from the road and whether the ₹50 Sikkim tourist fee is shown on the bill.

faqs.q: Which Gangtok hotels have Kanchenjunga views?
faqs.a: Only rooms facing north-west, on clear mornings mostly from October to April. Hotel Sonam Delek on Tibet Road sells rooms with windows facing the range, and Taj Guras Kutir describes Kanchenjunga views from its Pangthang site. Elsewhere it depends on floor and side, so ask for a mountain-facing room in writing and avoid paying a premium in the monsoon.

faqs.q: Is it better to stay on MG Marg or outside town?
faqs.a: On or near MG Marg is better for short stays and first visits: everything is walkable and you save on evening taxis, though street-facing rooms can be noisy until about 9 pm. Outside town is better for honeymoons, spa stays and longer trips, if you are happy to eat in and use a car for every outing.

Many do not. Gangtok is built on a ridge, and many hotels near MG Marg sit on steep lanes with stairs from the road and no lift. Branded hotels such as Lemon Tree, upmarket hotels and the forest resorts usually have lifts or level access. If you travel with elders or heavy bags, ask how many steps there are and where the car stops.

Yes. Registered homestays on the outskirts, towards Ranka, the Rumtek road and the villages below Tadong, cost about ₹1,200–2,500 per person a night with meals in 2026. Most have two to five rooms and home cooking, and are 20–40 minutes from town by car. Ask whether the homestay is registered with Sikkim Tourism and how the road is in the monsoon.

faqs.q: How early should I book a hotel in Gangtok?
faqs.a: Book 6–8 weeks ahead for October, especially the Durga Puja and Diwali weeks, for Christmas and New Year, and for May school holidays, when rooms near MG Marg sell out first. For March, late November and the monsoon months, 1–2 weeks is usually enough. If you are going to North Sikkim, fix Gangtok nights around the permit dates.

faqs.q: Where should I stay in Gangtok before an early flight?
faqs.a: Stay at Tadong on NH10, on the southern side of town, which saves 20–30 minutes on the drive to Bagdogra or NJP. If your flight leaves before about 1 pm, or it is the monsoon and NH10 may close, spend the last night in Siliguri instead. The drive down takes 4–5.5 hours in good conditions.
